request.spec:
On the sheet a transfer brought a person to, a steward can undo it on the same sheet-today they
arrived (a button on the row; any later day, anyone else, or a person who did not arrive by transfer
is refused with an error on the row): the person is transferred back to the sheet they came from by
exactly the transfer rules and lines, and this sheet then writes PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE name=<name>
to=<sheet id>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
On the sheet a transfer brought a person to, a steward can undo it on the same sheet-today they
arrived (a button on the row; any later day, anyone else, or a person who did not arrive by transfer
is refused with an error on the row): the person is transferred back to the sheet they came from by
exactly the transfer rules and lines, and this sheet then writes PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE name=<name>
to=<sheet id>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A steward can now undo a transfer on the sheet it brought the person to, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests (the new one plus three existing scenarios).

**How it behaves:**
- Each person row has an **Undo transfer** button (`person-transfer-undo`). It shows on every row so that someone who didn't arrive by transfer gets the error on their row rather than having no button.
- The undo goes through only when a steward presses it on the same sheet-today the person arrived. Anyone who isn't a steward, a later day, or a person who didn't arrive by transfer gets a row error (`person-error`) and nothing is written.
- When it goes through, the person is sent back by calling the existing transfer itself, so the rules and audit lines are exactly a transfer's. This sheet then writes `PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE … name=<name> to=<sheet id>`, followed by its rollup/totals lines.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration `V96__person_arrived_on.sql` adds an `arrived_on` column. A transfer now records the destination sheet's today there (`Person.transferredTo` takes it).
- **Server:** `PersonTransferService.undo(...)` holds the checks and audit records, exposed at `POST /api/people/transfer/undo` in `PersonController`.
- **Front end:** the button and an `undoTransfer` method in `features/people/people.ts`, matching how the Transfer button handles errors.

Two things to know:
- People transferred before this change have no arrival date stored, so their transfers can't be undone.
- A person who is sent back carries the other sheet as their origin and today as their arrival. That means a steward on the original sheet could undo the undo on the same day.
